name: National Voter Registration Day Block Party
why: Live music, art, brand freebies, and performances by Cure for Paranoia and Anania to celebrate National Voter Registration Day.

name: Free Outdoor Movies: High School Musical 2 and Fame
why: Outdoor double-feature of High School Musical 2 and Fame on the Williamsburg waterfront (weather permitting).

name: Get Out the Vote Postcard-Writing Hang
why: Informal postcard-writing gathering to boost democratic voter turnout in swing states, with drinks.

name: Astronomy on Tap: Celebrating the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope
venue: Somethin' Else at Dekalb Market Hall
why: Monthly science bar night where professional astronomers give short talks about the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, plus themed games.

name: Story-oke: Sing and Tell
why: Hybrid karaoke-storytelling show where performers share a true story about their connection to a song, then sing it live.

name: Doll Dressing: How Have Dolls Influenced Fashion?
why: Exhibition exploring the relationship between dolls and fashion through 170+ objects including fashion dolls alongside full-size garments; runs through Jan 3, 2027.

name: People in the City: Modern Portraits from the Baruch College Art Collection
why: Photos and prints depicting NYC inhabitants 1929–1986 by Alex Katz, Cindy Sherman, Andy Warhol, Gary Winogrand and others; runs through Dec 11.

name: Juilliard Fall Festival
why: Nine days of music, dance, and drama kicking off Juilliard's 2026–27 season; highlights include a Miles Davis salute, Steve Reich celebration, and Juilliard Orchestra; runs through Sep 25.

name: Gather Round: Let's Dance at Manhattan West
why: Free outdoor weekly dance and music series; this week Sekou McMiller hosts an intergenerational mambo social dance lesson with the Palladium Mambo Band.

name: Music for Enophiles
why: NYC band dedicated to performing Brian Eno's solo pop recordings from 1974–1977 plays Mercury Lounge.

name: Sunnyside Horror Society: Tribute to Tim Curry — IT Marathon
why: One-night marathon screening of the 1990 IT miniseries featuring Tim Curry as Pennywise, in tribute to the actor.

name: Adam Wade: Live in New York
why: 20-time Moth Story Slam winner Adam Wade performs three to four original stories from his catalog, with a rotating special guest.

name: Free Outdoor Movie: 2026 Oscar Nominated Animated Shorts
why: Outdoor screening of the 2026 Oscar-nominated animated short films (weather permitting; food/drink purchase required).

name: Cursed! The Power of Magic in the Ancient World
venue: Institute for the Study of the Ancient World at NYU
why: Exhibition of 50 ancient works—sculpture, ceramics, amulets, papyrus scrolls—examining magic's role in Mesopotamian, Egyptian, Greek, and Roman societies from 2000 BCE to 300 CE; runs through Dec 13.

name: Forest of Mononoke
why: Immersive installation of glowing acrylic sculptures inspired by Japanese folklore spirits, with a live performance by choreographer Peter Mercury; runs through Oct 14.

name: Yuen Woo-ping: The Number One Martial Arts Director Under the Sky
why: Retrospective of five decades of martial arts films directed by Yuen Woo-ping (Drunken Master, The Matrix, Crouching Tiger), with post-screening conversations on Sep 17 and Sep 18; runs through Oct 3.

name: The 100th Feast of San Gennaro
why: 100th annual Italian street festival with food vendors and live music on Mulberry Street, culminating in a procession featuring the statue of San Gennaro; runs through Sep 27.

name: Illumination Light Art Festival
why: Fifth annual outdoor light festival with 10+ large-scale light installations, projection mapping, DJs, performances, and food trucks at Wagner Park; runs Sep 17–19.

name: Drinks with Benefits Alcohol-Free Festival
why: Discovery festival with tastings from 60+ alcohol-free beverage brands—functional drinks, kanna, kava, adaptogens—plus guided meditation and a dance lounge.

name: Building the Future of NYC
why: Panel discussion on NYC city planning—affordability, aesthetics, and public space—with City Council member Shekar Krishnan, artist David Brooks, and architect Savina Romanos; part of the John Jay Iselin Memorial Lecture Series.

name: Fumbl Fest
why: Festival of film, music, and live performance aboard a historic floating museum in Red Hook, featuring the world premiere of a live-scored short film, dockside carnival games, and complimentary mocktails.

name: Facts Machine: Science, Comedy + Trivia — Space Science Edition
why: Scientists share stories behind their favorite space-science facts alongside trivia and drinking games; hosted by scientists and comedians.

name: Free Outdoor Movie: Zoolander
why: Free outdoor screening of Zoolander at the North Oculus Plaza (weather permitting).

name: Top Shelf Stories
why: An evening of carefully crafted personal storytelling hosted by Julia Whitehouse, with performers Lindsay Hand, Cody Lindquist, Justin Tyler, and Srilatha Rajamani.

name: The Hunger Games: Catching Fire Entirely from Memory
why: Theater company attempts to recreate The Hunger Games: Catching Fire on stage without scripts, rehearsals, or sobriety, incorporating audience-written lines and improvised deleted scenes.

name: Carly Rae Jepsen: Day and Night Album Release Party
why: Drag tribute show and listening party celebrating Carly Rae Jepsen's new album, with performances by Megami, Roque, and Atomic Annie.

name: The Mingle Games, Round 02
venue: Jaywalker at New York Distilling Co.
why: Social game night where you rotate through stations playing fast-paced games with strangers, with craft cocktails, beer, and dumplings at the New York Distilling Co. bar.

name: Claude Code Workshop with Provectus
why: Hands-on workshop where you build with Claude Code directly alongside engineering teams — not slides or demos, but shipping something real.

name: Robot Hackathon: Fine Motor Skills at Viam
why: Two-day hands-on hackathon where participants build physical AI applications with real robot arms, supported by Viam experts.

name: Harness Engineering & Model Wrangling Hackathon (NYC)
why: Build persistent, adaptive AI agents using MongoDB Atlas Vector Search and Agentic Memory in this in-person NYC hackathon.

name: MongoDB.local NYC: For Founders Building What's Next
price: Free for eligible founders (MongoDB for Startups Founder Pass)
why: Full-day event for NYC's AI community with technical sessions, live demos, workshops, and founder networking; eligible founders can attend free with Atlas credits and Voyage AI tokens.

name: NYC City Center Fall for Dance Festival
why: Beloved annual festival featuring 11 New York premieres and 7 international dance companies across two weeks at City Center; runs Sep 22–Oct 3.

name: MoMI After Dark: Lantern Gallery Tour
why: Lantern-lit tour through MoMI's darkened galleries spotlighting horror gems including The Exorcist exhibition, led by a Museum educator; tickets sell out quickly.

name: Overexposed: Art, Technology, and the Body
why: Exhibition of research-based films and contemporary artworks by 16 artists (Barbara Hammer, Ana Mendieta and others) examining the medical and political implications of X-ray imaging; runs through January 3.

name: Climate Film Festival Opening Night: House of Fish
why: East Coast premiere of House of Fish — documentary about Italian fisherman Paolo Fanciulli's underwater marble museum that protects the seabed from illegal trawling; director Santiago Burin des Roziers in person.

name: House of Dreams (1963, 16mm)
why: Rare screening of this never-distributed 1963 avant-garde horror short shot on 16mm — a frustrated author haunted by nightmares about a sinister house, from director Robert Berry.

name: Wild City + Wild Inside Screening
why: Daylong exploration of NYC's urban wildlife with Gotham Coyote and Gotham Whale, plus a screening of Penny Lane's new documentary Wild Inside about Flaco the Owl.

name: Your Name. (10th Anniversary Screening)
why: 10th anniversary screening of Makoto Shinkai's beloved animated fantasy about two high school students who mysteriously switch bodies on the eve of a rare cosmic event.

name: The Birds (Hitchcock)
why: Big-screen revival of Hitchcock's boldly music-free masterwork — begins as a romcom and escalates into an inexplicable, apocalyptic dread.

name: Responsive Signals: Artist Talks and Interactive Installations
source: Museum of the Moving Image / Art on Tezos
why: Artist talks and interactive installations by Jonas Lund, Yoshi Sodeoka, Kat Zhang, and Nick Fox-Gieg, during Armory Week, part of MoMI's year-long Tezos Foundation partnership.

name: Celebrating Jim Henson's 90th Birthday
why: Four-day celebration of Jim Henson's 90th birthday with special guests, screenings, puppet workshops, a collectible swap meet, and live music in the courtyard; Sep 24–27.

name: Orchard Recipes with Sam Van Aken
why: Artist Sam Van Aken cooks historical dishes using heirloom fruit harvested from his Open Orchard installation — varieties of New York native fruit largely lost to industrialized agriculture.

name: Climate Week 2026 at Governors Island
why: Climate Week NYC programming on Governors Island — public events and activations throughout the island during the global climate action week, Sep 20–27.

name: Civic Tech, Civic Voice: Rethinking How Communities Shape Cities
source: AIANY Social Science and Architecture Committee
why: Panel conversation examining how new civic technology shapes urban communities and who has a voice in how cities are designed.

name: AIANY Members and Friends Fall Happy Hour and Ballot Meeting
why: AIA New York's fall networking happy hour for members and friends at the Center for Architecture, with a chapter ballot meeting.

name: NYC Mass Timber Studio Launch: Accelerating Housing Development
why: Launch event for the NYC Mass Timber Studio initiative on accelerating housing development through mass timber construction.

name: How to Communicate Value and Resolve Conflicts: Interactive Workshop
why: Interactive professional workshop on communicating value and conflict resolution, geared toward architects and design professionals.

name: Walking Tour: Madison Avenue, High Fashion, and Historic Preservation
why: Guided walking tour exploring Madison Avenue's historic architecture alongside its identity as a high fashion corridor.

name: Walking Tour: The Architecture of Bryant Park
why: Guided architectural walking tour focusing on the buildings and design history surrounding Bryant Park.

name: AI Open Mic and Agentic Workshop
why: Five-hour AI open mic and hands-on agentic workflow workshop for architects and designers exploring AI applications in practice.

name: Walking Tour: Privately Owned Public Spaces (POPS) in Midtown North
why: Guided tour of Midtown North's privately owned public spaces — plazas and atriums built under NYC's zoning incentives — exploring access, design, and urban policy.

name: Humanist Modernity: Maciej and Stanisława Nowicki
why: Exhibition opening at the Center for Architecture presenting the work of Polish-American architects Maciej and Stanisława Nowicki.

name: Dark Matter U: Justice, Pedagogy, Design
why: Exhibition opening at the Center for Architecture exploring the intersections of justice, pedagogy, and design.

name: Why Design?
why: Exhibition opening at the Center for Architecture posing fundamental questions about the purpose and role of design.

name: On This Spot at The Cooper Union: Five Pioneering Women Artists
venue: Frederick P. Rose Auditorium, Cooper Union
why: Five short documentaries profiling Cooper Union alumni artists Eva Hesse, Lee Krasner, Marcia Marcus, Margaret Morton, and Maria Lassnig, with contextual remarks on their lives and legacies.

name: Bernard Tschumi: Circular
venue: Frederick P. Rose Auditorium, Cooper Union
why: Architect Bernard Tschumi (Parc de la Villette, Acropolis Museum) presents projects and ideas tracing his practice's evolution, followed by a conversation with Cooper Union's architecture dean.

name: Beyond the Rubble: DSNY and the Recovery After 9/11
why: Short documentary about NYC Sanitation's little-known role in the post-9/11 recovery at Ground Zero and Fresh Kills, followed by a panel discussion with DSNY insiders.

name: Shakespeare and Verdi's Macbeth: Discussion and Performance
why: Met Opera director Louisa Proske and Shakespeare scholar James Shapiro discuss parallels between Shakespeare's Macbeth and Verdi's opera; performances by Met cast members including soprano Felicia Moore and baritone Quinn Kelsey.

name: Native Voices Karenna — Lay Our Vibration Down
why: New York-stage premieres of two short operas — Trials and Tears and Sacajawea: Woman of Many Names — by Grammy-nominated cellist-composer Dawn Avery (Mohawk), with music direction by Danielle Olana Jagelski.

name: Irish Literature: History & Myth Since 1798 (Exhibition Opening)
venue: New-York Historical Society, Luman Reed Galleries
why: Exhibition exploring Irish literature as a vehicle for national identity and political transformation — rare books, manuscripts, broadsheets, playbills, drawings and prints from American collector Leonard Milberg's archive.

name: Docent-Led Gallery Tour: Democracy Matters
why: Docent-led gallery tour through the Democracy Matters exhibition; also offered Sep 25.

name: Supremacy: How Rule by the Court Replaced Government by the People
why: Harvard Law professors Nikolas Bowie and Daphna Renan trace how "we the people" became a foundational fallacy in American constitutional history, in conversation with law professor Kate Shaw.

name: History by a Hair: Thomas Jefferson, Sally Hemings, & Solving a 200-Year-Old Mystery
why: Smithsonian's Richard Kurin recounts the 15-year forensic investigation — DNA, genealogy, archaeology — sparked by a strand of hair in Jefferson's Bible to settle whether he fathered Sally Hemings's children.

name: A Nation in Conversation: David Blight and Khalil Gibran Muhammad
why: Civil War and Reconstruction historians David Blight and Khalil Gibran Muhammad discuss how contested narratives of American history shape our understanding of democracy, citizenship, and identity today.

name: Selected Shorts: The Five Boroughs
why: Cynthia Nixon hosts a literary reading event with Bobby Cannavale, Sonia Manzano, and others — stories from all five boroughs offering five unique vantage points on New York City.

name: Grand Central Terminal Tour (MAS Docent-Led)
time: Multiple dates and times — see website
source: Municipal Art Society of New York
why: Ongoing docent-led MAS tours of Grand Central Terminal; multiple weekly slots. One of NYC's most storied architectural interiors.

name: Greenpoint in Brooklyn Walking Tour
source: Municipal Art Society of New York
why: MAS guide Zack Rhodes leads a walking tour through Greenpoint, Brooklyn — historic architecture, industrial past, and the neighborhood's Polish and artistic heritage.

name: Sunday Morning in Greenwich Village Walking Tour
source: Municipal Art Society of New York
why: MAS tour director Ted Mineau leads a Sunday morning architectural and historical walk through Greenwich Village.

name: New York: A Documentary Film — Screening + Panel (Episodes 9 & 10)
venue: Museum of the City of New York
source: Museum of the City of New York
why: Advance preview screening of two new chapters of Ric Burns's 17½-hour documentary series — "The Future of Cities" (Episodes 9–10) — followed by a panel with Burns and co-creator James Sanders.

name: Art as Care: Hospital Murals in Pediatric Healthcare
venue: Museum of the City of New York
source: Museum of the City of New York
why: Panel with artists, advocates, and NYC Health + Hospitals leaders examining what ambitious public art does for children in city hospitals — from a 1938 Alice mural at Gouverneur Hospital to today. Presented alongside the Another Wonderland exhibition.

name: He Built This City: Joe Macken's Model (Exhibition)
venue: Museum of the City of New York
source: Museum of the City of New York
why: 21-year labor of love: Queens-born Joe Macken built a monumental handmade model of all of New York City using balsa wood, cardboard, and glue — one of the most ambitious representations of the city ever created.

name: Exclusive Tour Inside the Woolworth Building: NYC's Cathedral of Commerce
why: Rare interior access to the Woolworth Building — the 1913 skyscraper once called 'the Cathedral of Commerce' — exploring its ornate lobby, historic elevators, and building secrets.

name: Inside The Players: Rare Look Inside Edwin Booth's Untouched Bedroom
why: Access inside The Players, the legendary Gramercy Park club founded by Edwin Booth, including a rare look at Booth's preserved private bedroom — a room unchanged since the 1800s.

name: The Secret Eats of Arthur Avenue Food Crawl: The Bronx's Little Italy
why: Guided food crawl through Arthur Avenue's Italian markets, bakeries, and delis — the Bronx neighborhood that's remained more authentically Italian than Little Italy for decades.

name: Exclusive Trip Inside the Loew's Valencia: NYC's First "Wonder Theatre"
why: Rare access inside Loew's Valencia, one of the five opulent 1929 Loew's Wonder Theatres — now a Pentecostal church preserving its extraordinary Spanish Baroque movie-palace interior.

name: The Garbage That Built New York: A Walk Through NYC's Trash & Rat History
why: Walking tour tracing how NYC's landfill and trash history literally built neighborhoods — and introduced the rats that never left.

name: East Village, Rocks! Exploring the Neighborhood's Rock Music Legacy
why: Walking tour of the East Village's legendary rock history — CBGB, the Velvet Underground, Patti Smith, Television — exploring the neighborhood that incubated punk and new wave.

name: Behind-the-Scenes @ Lincoln Center: Extended Tour Inside Iconic Halls
venue: Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts
why: Extended backstage tour of Lincoln Center's performance halls — Alice Tully Hall, Avery Fisher/David Geffen Hall, the Metropolitan Opera — including normally off-limits areas.

name: Exclusive Truffle 101 & Hands-On Tasting @ The Urbani Truffle Lab NYC
why: Hands-on truffle education and tasting at Urbani's NYC lab — the world's largest truffle distributor — covering varieties, history, and how to use fresh truffles.

name: Private Tour @ Lotus Garden, Hidden Rooftop Garden
why: Private access to Lotus Garden, one of NYC's best-kept secrets — a lush half-acre community garden atop a parking garage on the Upper West Side, normally closed to the public.

name: Secrets of the East River: NYC's Hidden Infrastructure by Ferry
why: Ferry tour revealing the East River's hidden infrastructure — power stations, sewage treatment plants, islands, and engineering marvels visible only from the water.

name: Behind-the-Scenes @ Temple Emanu-El: One of the World's Largest Synagogues
why: Behind-the-scenes tour of Temple Emanu-El — the largest synagogue in the world by sanctuary size — including rarely accessed spaces and its century of history on Fifth Avenue.

name: Rare Look Inside M&S Schmalberg: NYC's Last Custom Fabric Flower Factory
why: Rare access inside M&S Schmalberg, the last custom fabric flower factory in NYC — supplying haute couture houses for over 100 years, still hand-crafting silk flowers using techniques unchanged since 1920.

name: Walking Brooklyn's Gowanus Canal: From Toxic Past to Luxury Living
why: Walking tour of the Gowanus Canal's transformation — from industrial Superfund site to one of Brooklyn's hottest real estate markets — exploring who wins and who loses in urban remediation.

name: Gallery Opening: Land, Liberty and the Pursuit of Happiness
venue: The Old Stone House, Washington Park
source: NYC Parks / The Old Stone House
why: Opening reception for a new exhibition at the Old Stone House — the reconstructed 1699 Dutch farmhouse in Park Slope that served as a pivot point in the Battle of Brooklyn.

name: Climate Week NYC: Nature Your City Talks at NYBG
venue: New York Botanical Garden, The Bronx
why: Week of talks with leading urban ecologists and conservationists exploring how to bring nature back into cities — part of Climate Week NYC 2026 programming at NYBG.

name: NYBG 5K Fun Run (Climate Week)
venue: New York Botanical Garden, The Bronx
why: 3.1-mile road-and-trail 5K through the Garden's late-season scenery — old-growth Thain Family Forest, maple collection, Stone Mill, Enid Haupt Conservatory — closing out Climate Week NYC.

name: Día de los Muertos at NYBG
venue: New York Botanical Garden, The Bronx
why: Month-long NYBG Día de los Muertos celebration: vibrant marigold blooms, a community ofrenda, puppets, crafts, and music — running October 3 through November 2.

name: Brooklyn Botanic Garden Fall Harvest Festival
price: Paid (BBG member discount; VIP tickets available)
why: Annual fall festival at BBG: live music, beer and cider garden (Talea, Grimm, Liquid Fables), pumpkin carving demo by Maniac Pumpkin Carvers, cider press, Redhawk Native American Arts Council performers, costume parade — all in peak fall foliage.

name: The Fling at Fort Greene Park (25th Anniversary Benefit)
why: Annual outdoor benefit party in Fort Greene Park to toast 2026 Community Heroes and kick off the Conservancy's 25th anniversary — jazz ensemble by Brooklyn Music School, then DJ Saint James Joy keeping the dance floor moving; BYO picnic or pre-order catered meal.

name: Fabric Pocket Altars Workshop (Healing Arts Week)
venue: Brooklyn Craft Company — Lower Manhattan location (225 Broadway)
why: Art therapy textile workshop creating personalized fabric pocket altars — part of UNGA Healing Arts Week, the Jameel Arts & Health Lab / WHO initiative on the intersection of arts and wellbeing (Sep 19–26).

name: Beaded Embroidery Workshop
venue: Brooklyn Craft Company — Lower Manhattan (225 Broadway)
why: Hands-on beaded embroidery workshop at Brooklyn Craft Company's Lower Manhattan pop-up; also offered Oct 13.

name: Backstage Metropolitan Opera Tour
price: Paid ($15 off for Untapped Insiders/Explorers members)
why: Exclusive backstage access to the Met Opera's prop/wig/costume/carpentry shops, dressing rooms, the auditorium, and Chagall-muraled lobby — new dates running September through January.

name: Battle of Harlem Heights Revolutionary Walking Tour
why: Walking tour of the Battle of Harlem Heights (September 16, 1776) — the pivotal Revolution skirmish that boosted Patriot morale after the disastrous Battle of Brooklyn, fought in what is now northern Manhattan.

name: Private Tour: The Last Surviving Mansion of Pelham Bay Park (Bronx)
why: Rare private tour of the last mid-19th century estate in Pelham Bay Park — mansion, carriage house, and bucolic grounds; once the official summer office of Mayor Fiorello LaGuardia.

name: 1960s Pop in NYC: Brill Building to The Beatles Walking Tour
why: Walking tour through Midtown Manhattan's 1959–64 pop music nerve center — the Brill Building, record labels, publishing houses, and demo studios that produced hits for everyone from the Shirelles to the Beatles.

name: NY Art Book Fair 2026 Opening Night (20th Anniversary)
why: 20th anniversary NY Art Book Fair opening night at MoMA PS1 — music by SHYBOI + A.B.E.L.A, bar by Symone, limited-edition artwork. Fair continues Sep 25–27 with hundreds of international artists, publishers, and booksellers.

name: NYC Transit Museum Bus Festival
venue: Emily Warren Roebling Plaza, Brooklyn Bridge Park
why: Annual outdoor festival celebrating NYC bus history with vintage buses on display, activities, and transit memorabilia — free admission at Brooklyn Bridge Park's Roebling Plaza.

name: The Potential for Life Next Door — Sara Seager on Venus
venue: The Explorers Club, 46 E 70th St, Manhattan
why: MIT planetary scientist Sara Seager presents her research on the possibility of microbial life floating in Venus's sulfuric acid clouds — one of the most provocative ongoing debates in astrobiology.

name: Nuisance Bear — Film Screening + Panel
venue: The Explorers Club, 46 E 70th St, Manhattan
why: Screening of Nuisance Bear — a documentary on human-bear conflict and wildlife management — followed by a panel discussion at the Explorers Club.

name: The Future of Our Blue Planet — WEF Ocean Action Panel
venue: The Explorers Club, 46 E 70th St, Manhattan
why: Panel on ocean conservation and climate futures with World Economic Forum Friends of Ocean Action — convened at the Explorers Club during Climate Week NYC.

name: Reimagining Filipino Brooklyn — Talk + Film
venue: Center for Brooklyn History, 128 Pierrepont St
why: Talk and short film exploring the history and contemporary culture of Brooklyn's Filipino community — part of CBH's ongoing series on borough immigrant histories.

name: Brooklyn Trivia with Trivia Masters
venue: Center for Brooklyn History, 128 Pierrepont St
why: Evening of Brooklyn-themed trivia hosted by Trivia Masters at the Center for Brooklyn History — competitive but casual, no team required.

name: Haunted Brooklyn Panel
venue: Center for Brooklyn History, 128 Pierrepont St
why: Panel discussion on Brooklyn's haunted history — ghost lore, legends, and the real histories behind them — timed to Halloween week.

name: Battle of Brooklyn Exhibition Tours at CBH
venue: Center for Brooklyn History, 128 Pierrepont St
why: Guided tours of CBH's ongoing Battle of Brooklyn exhibition — the 250th anniversary of the 1776 battle that nearly ended the American Revolution, fought across what is now Brooklyn.

name: Beaux Arts Ball 2026: Home Sweet Home
venue: Andrew Freedman Home, Grand Concourse, The Bronx
price: Paid (party tickets; dinner tickets; member discount available)
why: Annual NYC design community bash at the storied Andrew Freedman Home on the Bronx's Grand Concourse — commissioned installation by TAKK (Mireia Luzárraga & Alejandro Muiño), lighting by Joel Fitzpatrick Studio, DJs Bojaq and Madre Guia.

name: To Explore is to Lead: Climate Vanguard (Michael Mann, Johan Rockström + more)
venue: The Explorers Club, 46 E 70th St, Manhattan
why: Top climate scientists and leaders — Michael Mann, Johan Rockström, Gail Gallie — share leadership insights from the climate vanguard, part of Climate Week NYC at Explorers Club HQ. Full week of programming Sep 21–25.

name: Plant Life: Film Screening + Climate-Resilient Agriculture Talk (Salk Institute)
venue: The Explorers Club, 46 E 70th St, Manhattan
why: Screening of Plant Life — documentary on pioneering botanist Dr. Joanne Chory — followed by a conversation with Salk Institute scientists on harnessing plants to draw down atmospheric carbon.

name: Wilkes Climate Innovation Prize Announcement (XPrize / Univ. of Utah)
venue: The Explorers Club, 46 E 70th St, Manhattan
why: Live announcement of the Wilkes Climate Innovation Prize winner — a bold-solutions award from the Wilkes Center (U of Utah) in partnership with XPrize targeting the climate/energy/economy nexus.

name: Art & Environmental Impact with Christie's (ClientEarth, The King's Trust + more)
venue: The Explorers Club, 46 E 70th St, Manhattan
why: Closing night of Climate Week at Explorers Club: Christie's hosts a conversation with ClientEarth, The King's Trust, and Endangered Rainforest Rescue on how art can drive environmental action — policy, conservation, and public engagement.

name: Colin Stetson & Brìghde Chaimbeul + Space Lady + Clarice Jensen
venue: Pioneer Works, 159 Pioneer St, Red Hook
why: Rare duo performance of Colin Stetson and Brìghde Chaimbeul's album All the Light in the World, plus an extremely rare NYC appearance by the legendary Space Lady (Susan Dietrich Schneider), and cellist Clarice Jensen.

name: Observe the Moon Night at Pioneer Works Pier
venue: Portside NewYork Pier, Pioneer Works, Red Hook
why: Evening of lunar science, storytelling, and first-quarter Moon observation from the Red Hook waterfront pier alongside the historic tanker Mary A. Whalen — part of Pioneer Works' Oceans Season.

name: Science & Society: The Ocean Frontier (Ayana Elizabeth Johnson, Diva Amon)
venue: Pioneer Works, 159 Pioneer St, Red Hook
why: Marine biologist and policy expert Ayana Elizabeth Johnson hosts deep-sea biologist Dr. Diva Amon and climate investor Ben Wolkon on ocean industrialization — the science, policy, and stakes of getting it wrong. Part of Ocean Season.

name: A Winged Victory for the Sullen + Pan•American (Two Nights)
venue: Pioneer Works Main Hall, 159 Pioneer St, Red Hook
why: Rare two-night engagement at Pioneer Works from the ambient duo A Winged Victory for the Sullen — luminous, cinematic soundscapes in the soaring Main Hall — with Pan•American opening.

name: Pioneer Works Fall Exhibitions: Siphon / Child/ren of the Bloom / There is no me without you
time: Open during gallery hours through Nov/Dec 2026
venue: Pioneer Works, 159 Pioneer St, Red Hook
why: Three major new fall exhibitions: Tuomas A. Laitinen's Siphon (immersive 8K video of octopus camouflage + spatial sound), LaJuné McMillian's Child/ren of the Bloom (interactive phytoplankton/bioluminescence installation), and Finnegan Shannon's There is no me without you (disability art / mechanized conveyor installation).

name: The Atlantic Festival & The American Reading Crisis
venue: Brooklyn Public Library, Central Library, Dweck Center
why: Atlantic staff writer Rose Horowitch, BPL president Linda Johnson, and author Hilary Leichter discuss the decline of reading culture; then author Tayari Jones on literature's power to cultivate empathy and challenge American narratives.

name: Dream Symposium 2026 (Philosophy, Psychology, Art & Science of Dreaming)
venue: Brooklyn Public Library, Library for Arts & Culture
why: Three-day BPL symposium exploring dreaming from four angles — philosophy, psychology, art, and science — for dreamers, artists, and inquiring minds.

name: Hello Darknuss: Reflections on the Intergalactic Greg Tate (Questlove, Arthur Jafa, dream hampton, Jelani Cobb)
venue: Brooklyn Public Library, Central Library, Dweck Center
why: Special forum celebrating the life and work of the late music writer Greg Tate — Arthur Jafa, Questlove, dream hampton, and Jelani Cobb gather to discuss his cosmic legacy. Moderated by Daphne A. Brooks.

name: On Artistic Freedom: A Panel Discussion (Banned Books Week)
venue: Brooklyn Public Library, Central Library, Dweck Center
why: Banned Books Week panel with artist-author Christopher Myers, film producer Karin Chien, and Namrata Tripathi (Kokila Books) on artistic freedom — moderated by Hyperallergic's Hrag Vartanian.

name: Classical Interludes: Ljova and WhEE (Where Else Ensemble)
venue: Brooklyn Public Library, Central Library, Dweck Center
why: Live concert with Ljova and the Where Else Ensemble: folkloric poetry set to music performed in Russian (with English translation), plus original Yiddish folk songs and music from Central Asia.

name: New Climate Futures @ Newlab (Largest NY Climate Week Event)
venue: Newlab, 19 Morris Ave, Brooklyn Navy Yard
why: Largest event of NY Climate Week: 70+ climate tech startup demos, founders, investors, and policymakers under one roof at Newlab in the Brooklyn Navy Yard.

name: Space Apps NYC: Exploring NASA Challenges
venue: NYU Tandon School of Engineering, 370 Jay St, Brooklyn
why: Annual NASA international space apps challenge kickoff at NYU Tandon — explore this year's NASA challenges with Twilio and Open Space; part of the global 48-hour hackathon.

name: Open House New York Weekend (OHNY)
why: Annual weekend of free access to hundreds of NYC buildings normally closed to the public — from infrastructure to landmarks, private residences to cultural institutions — the city's premier architecture and design event.

name: The New Yorker Festival
why: Annual New Yorker Festival weekend of conversations, performances, and events with writers, artists, scientists, and newsmakers — one of NYC's flagship fall cultural events.

name: Diwali on the Hudson
why: Diwali celebration on the Hudson River — festival of lights, music, and community gathering on the waterfront.

name: The Cocktails of the Waldorf Astoria
time: Various dates this fall; see website
venue: Brooklyn Brainery, 190 Underhill Ave, Prospect Heights
why: Brooklyn Brainery class on the history and recipes of the iconic Waldorf Astoria cocktail canon — from the Rob Roy to the Waldorf Cocktail — taught by a cocktail historian.

name: How to Research in the Age of AI (Sarah Lohman)
time: October 1; see website for exact time
venue: Brooklyn Brainery, 190 Underhill Ave, Prospect Heights
why: In-person class with food historian and author Sarah Lohman on effective research techniques in the era of AI — practical skills for writers, journalists, and curious researchers.

name: Sinister Scents and Perfumed Potions Workshop
time: Various dates this fall; see website
venue: Brooklyn Brainery, 190 Underhill Ave, Prospect Heights
why: Hands-on Brooklyn Brainery workshop blending dark botanicals, resins, and mysterious notes into wearable scents — perfumery with a gothic-autumn edge.
